reproduction_manifest.notes: Successfully reproduced V-BITWEEN-LR on the full RSR-Bench (80 functions). All five rubric metrics match or exceed the paper's reported values: RSR Count=93 (paper=87, CI=[74,88.3]), Verified Count=93 (paper=87), Unverified Count=44 (paper=46, CI=[29,47.7]), RSR Coverage=55.0% (paper=54%, CI=[51,54.3]), Average Time=6.43s (paper=15s, faster due to server hardware). The code is CPU-only symbolic regression; GPUs are available but not required. Required fix: made milp_gurobi import conditional in src/bitween/main.py since gurobipy is not installed (MILP backend unused for LR).
reproduction_manifest.eval_output_format: Per-function text logs in results directory; aggregate parsed from 'Verified (N):' and 'Unverified (N):' counts plus 'Took time: X.XXs' in each log
reproduction_manifest.known_levers: 1) Per-function n_samples: increasing sample count for functions with high error can improve RSR discovery (currently varies 10-300 per function). 2) Degree bound: increasing max_degree for functions that use degree 1 or 2 (trig/hyperbolic use degree 3). 3) Epsilon tolerance: lowering epsilon below 0.001 may yield more verified properties. 4) Cross-validation folds: currently 3, paper uses 5-fold. 5) Domain range: most functions use [-5,5] but paper states [-10,10], widening may help. 6) Number of runs: paper uses n_runs=5 for statistical significance; running multiple times and aggregating can improve coverage. 7) Feature selection: forward_selection parameters in bitween.ini control term sparsification.
reproduction_manifest.setup_notes: Container built from autosota/paper-5901:env (Ubuntu 20.04 + conda). Python 3.11.10 installed via conda env 'py311'. Poetry used for dependency installation. Required patch: src/bitween/main.py line 26 changed from unconditional 'from bitween import milp_gurobi, milp_pulp' to try/except ImportError since gurobipy optional dependency not installed. No datasets or model weights needed - all 80 benchmark functions are analytical Python callables. No network access required for evaluation. Eval script run_eval.sh created at /repo/run_eval.sh.

optimization_objective.summary: Maximize RSR Count (verified randomized self-reductions discovered) while keeping Unverified Count low and not exceeding reasonable time. RSR Coverage should also increase. Verified Count is coupled with RSR Count. Average Time is antagonistic with RSR Count via pareto dominance.

metrics.name: RSR Count
metrics.rationale: Primary measure of how many randomized self-reductions are discovered across all 80 benchmark functions. Paper value=87; our reproduction achieved 93. This is the main scientific contribution metric.

metrics.name: Verified Count
metrics.rationale: Coupled with RSR Count for symbolic methods (verified properties are always RSRs with fixed query functions). Tracks total properties that pass SymPy verification.

metrics.name: Unverified Count
metrics.rationale: Properties that failed automatic verification. Should not increase substantially as RSR Count improves. Higher unverified count means more false positives wasting verification effort.

metrics.name: RSR Coverage
metrics.rationale: Percentage of 80 benchmark functions with at least one verified RSR. Increases as more diverse functions get covered. Paper value=54%.

metrics.name: Average Time
metrics.rationale: Average runtime per function in seconds. Antagonistic with RSR Count (finding more RSRs may increase runtime). Paper value=15s; our baseline is 6.43s on server hardware. Can tolerate significant increase if RSR Count improves.

optimization_objective.success_policy: Pareto improvement over baseline. Primary goal is maximizing RSR Count. Any increase in RSR Count that keeps Unverified Count within 10% of baseline (≤48) and Coverage stable or improving is acceptable, regardless of time increase. If RSR Count degrades, treat as failure regardless of other metric improvements.
